answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 17 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the ferrous solution is checked at the beacon gate and logged, the relic audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch hence pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. A farm of 39 pays that 225 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
